states.title: Prep Confit Garlic
states.direction: Peel garlic cloves and place in a small oven-safe dish. Pour olive oil over cloves until fully submerged. Preheat oven to 250°F (120°C).
states.exit_condition: Garlic cloves fully submerged in oil, oven preheating

notes.text: Can be done up to 2 weeks ahead — store confit garlic submerged in oil in the fridge. Flavor improves over the first few days.

Food safety: refrigerate confit garlic within 2 hours. Never store at room temperature — garlic submerged in oil is anaerobic, exactly what C. botulinum needs. Fridge temps halt toxin production. Safe up to 7 days refrigerated (FDA guideline). Once garlic is removed from oil and chopped, the anaerobic seal is broken and botulism risk is over.
Make-ahead overnight: confit evening before, cool, refrigerate submerged in oil. Next morning pull garlic out, chop, fold into dough. Flavor actually improves overnight.

states.title: Bake Confit Garlic
states.direction: Bake garlic in oil at 250°F (120°C) for 2 hours until cloves are pale golden and completely soft.
states.exit_condition: Garlic cloves pale golden, knife slides through with zero resistance

notes.text: Stovetop alternative: lowest heat for 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Watch for garlic darkening past pale gold.

states.title: Chop Confit Garlic
states.direction: Remove garlic cloves from oil with a slotted spoon. Cool briefly, then rough chop into small pieces. Reserve the garlic-infused oil separately.
states.exit_condition: Garlic rough chopped, confit oil reserved in separate container

notes.text: The confit oil is liquid gold — use 1-2 tbsp in place of some dough butter for extra garlic depth, or save for cooking.

states.title: Make Tangzhong
states.direction: Combine water and bread flour in a small saucepan. Whisk until smooth with no lumps. Heat over medium-low, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens to a thick paste (about 2 minutes). Remove from heat and cool completely.
states.exit_condition: Thick, glossy paste that leaves trails when stirred. Cooled to room temperature.

notes.text: Tangzhong gelatinizes starch, trapping moisture for a softer crumb that stays fresh 3-4 days. This is the technique that gives these buns their signature pillowy texture.

states.title: Bloom Yeast
states.direction: Warm milk to 110°F (43°C). Stir in 4g sugar until dissolved, then sprinkle yeast over surface. Let sit until foamy, about 5 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Yeast mixture foamy and actively bubbling

states.title: Mix Dough
states.direction: Combine bread flour, remaining sugar, gochujang, and salt in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, stir egg and melted butter into the cooled tangzhong. Add the tangzhong mixture and yeast-milk mixture to the dry ingredients. Stir with a rubber spatula until a shaggy dough forms.
states.exit_condition: Shaggy dough formed, no dry flour visible. Dough will be sticky — this is expected.

notes.text: Gochujang adds hidden water (~44% moisture) and salt (~8%). The dough will feel wetter than typical enriched dough — don't add extra flour yet.

states.title: Knead Dough
states.direction: Transfer dough to a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky, about 8-10 minutes by hand. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with dough hook on medium-low for 6-8 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth and elastic, springs back when poked, no longer sticking to hands or counter

notes.text: If dough remains very sticky after 5 minutes of kneading, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time. The tangzhong and gochujang both add moisture.

states.title: First Rise
states.direction: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm spot until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
states.exit_condition: Dough has doubled in volume — poke test: finger indent fills back slowly

states.title: Fold in Confit Garlic
states.direction: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently press to deflate. Spread chopped confit garlic evenly over the surface. Fold dough over itself several times to distribute garlic throughout.
states.exit_condition: Garlic pieces visibly distributed throughout dough, no large unworked pockets

notes.text: Don't over-knead — just fold enough to distribute. The garlic pieces should create pockets of flavor in the finished crumb.

states.title: Divide & Shape
states.direction: Divide dough into 75g pieces (about 10 buns). Roll each piece into a tight ball: cup your hand over the dough and roll in a circular motion on an unfloured surface, tucking the dough under to create surface tension.
states.exit_condition: All buns shaped into smooth, taut balls with visible surface tension

states.title: Second Rise
states.direction: Arrange buns in prepared pan, leaving small gaps between each. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let rise until buns are puffy and nearly touching.
states.exit_condition: Buns are puffy, nearly doubled, and just touching each other in the pan

reminders.prompt: How do the buns look? Puffy and touching?

states.title: Score & Egg Wash
states.direction: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Using a sharp knife or lame, score a simple cross or slash pattern on top of each bun (about 0.5cm deep). Lightly beat the remaining egg and brush over the tops of all buns.
states.exit_condition: All buns scored and evenly coated with egg wash

notes.text: Score gently — enriched dough deflates easily. The scores are decorative, not structural.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25-30 minutes, rotating pan halfway through, until buns are deep golden brown.
states.exit_condition: Deep golden brown on top, internal temperature reads 190°F (88°C)

notes.text: Gochujang's sugars accelerate browning — check at 20 minutes and tent with foil if the tops are getting too dark before the interior is done.

states.title: Cool in Pan
states.direction: Transfer pan to a wire rack. Let buns cool in the pan for 10 minutes before applying glaze or serving.
states.exit_condition: Buns cool enough to handle but still warm — ideal temperature for glaze absorption

states.title: Mix Honey-Soy Glaze
states.direction: Stir together honey and light soy sauce in a small bowl until combined. Melt butter separately.
states.exit_condition: Honey-soy mixture smooth and uniform, butter melted

notes.text: This glaze is optional but community-tested — Sophie Bamford's most popular upgrade to Dylan's original. Sweet-salty-umami without tipping into dessert territory.

states.title: Apply Glaze & Finish
states.direction: Brush honey-soy mixture over warm buns. Then brush melted butter on top. Sprinkle sesame seeds over all buns.
states.exit_condition: All buns coated with glaze, butter, and sesame seeds. Glossy finish visible.

notes.text: Order matters: honey-soy first (soaks in), then butter (seals and shines), then sesame seeds (stick to butter).
If making ahead: store unglazed. Reheat buns, then glaze while hot for best results.

techniques.name: Tangzhong (Water Roux)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official recipe + all 4 copycat recreations
techniques.rationale: Pre-gelatinized starch doubles moisture retention, producing soft pillowy crumb that stays fresh 3-4 days

techniques.name: Gochujang in Dough
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official + 3/4 copycats mix into dough, not just filling
techniques.rationale: Distributes fermented chili flavor and color throughout. ~8% baker's percentage for balanced heat

techniques.name: Confit Garlic (folded after first rise)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Dylan's official method — garlic folded in post-rise to preserve gluten
techniques.rationale: Mellow, sweet garlic that holds shape as pockets in the crumb. Post-rise fold avoids disrupting gluten network

techniques.name: Honey-Soy Post-Bake Glaze
techniques.rationale: Sweet-salty-umami finish. Butter layer prevents stickiness. Most popular non-original addition
